01 / THE QUESTION

The business context.

Finding the right information inside organizational documents takes time. The project explores how a local retrieval system can help users access relevant knowledge and verify answers against source material while keeping documents in an offline environment.

02 / EXPLORE THE WORK

LOCAL KNOWLEDGE. CONNECTED.
OFFLINE BY DESIGNHover or focus to pause

EXPLORE THE ARCHITECTURE

How a question becomes a grounded answer.

Organize the knowledge

Enterprise documents are prepared and indexed so their content can be retrieved. This is the foundation for connecting a user’s question to source material.

Architecture walkthrough, not a live AI chat. No documents or questions are uploaded.

03 / THE APPROACH

From question to evidence.

01

Index

Prepare and index enterprise documents for retrieval.

02

Retrieve

Use semantic search to identify passages relevant to a user’s question.

03

Rerank

Reorder candidate passages to improve the relevance of the context supplied to the model.

04

Generate

Use a local language model to produce a contextual answer, with source material available for verification.

04 / WHAT I LEARNED

The useful part of the analysis.

01

Evaluate the experience

The pilot assessed usability, answer quality, usefulness, and traceability, with a reported mean rating of 4.29/5.

02

Connect architecture to workflow

Retrieval and generation configurations were compared to study practical access to organizational knowledge.

03

Keep sources inspectable

The business value depends on users being able to examine supporting material, not simply receive fluent text.

Enterprise AI should make knowledge usable while supporting privacy, traceability, and careful human review.

05 / SCOPE & LIMITATIONS

What the evidence does—and doesn’t—say.

The 4.29/5 result is a pilot evaluation rating. It is not an accuracy percentage, a security certification, or proof of an organization-wide efficiency improvement.
